badge.hint: {appName} found signs of ransomware in this restore point. Open it for the reasons.

object.hint: The newest restore point shows signs of ransomware. Check the system before you restore, and restore from a restore point without findings.

lastClean.title: The newest restore point is suspicious
lastClean.description: Restore points from {since} on show signs of ransomware. The newest restore point without findings is from {time}.
lastClean.pick: Use the last clean restore point
lastClean.none: Every restore point that was judged shows signs of ransomware. Restore with care and check the files before you use them.
lastClean.selected: This restore point is suspicious. The newest one without findings is from {time}.
lastClean.selectedNone: This restore point is suspicious, and no restore point without findings is left.

details.title: Signs of ransomware
details.limits: {appName} judges what the backup saw change: amounts, names and a few sampled files. A finding is a reason to look, not a proof, and a clean result does not prove that no files were encrypted.
details.loadFailed: The findings could not be loaded.

findings.change_rate_items: {value} new or changed files, usually about {baseline} (alert above {threshold})
findings.mass_deletions: {value} files deleted, {share} of the files before
findings.mass_renames: {value} files renamed to another extension, {share} of the files ({examples})
findings.known_extensions: {value} files with a known ransomware extension ({examples})
findings.ransom_notes: {value} files named like a ransom note ({examples})
findings.high_entropy: {value} of the sampled files look encrypted ({examples})

falseAlarm.title: Mark as a false alarm?
falseAlarm.description: The restore point then counts as clean, and its numbers join the baseline of {object}, so the same amount of change no longer raises an alert. The next finding is announced again. This is recorded in the audit log.
falseAlarm.notePlaceholder: For example: planned move of the project folders
falseAlarm.failed: It could not be marked as a false alarm
falseAlarm.revokeFailed: The false alarm could not be undone

settings.title: Ransomware detection
settings.description: After every backup of a machine, file share, Proxmox VE guest, mailbox or OneDrive, {appName} compares what changed with the object's own history and with known ransomware names. A suspicious restore point is marked and announced once per episode (event "Suspicious backup").
settings.enabled: Check restore points for signs of ransomware
settings.baselineRuns: Earlier clean restore points in the baseline
settings.minBaselineRuns: Restore points needed before the amount of change is judged
settings.changeRateHint: A run alerts when it lies the given number of deviations above the object's median, is at least the given multiple of it, and reaches the minimum.
settings.minItems: Minimum of new or changed files
settings.deletionsMinShare: Minimum share of the files before (percent)
settings.saveFailed: The thresholds could not be saved
settings.loadFailed: The thresholds could not be loaded.
settings.readOnly: Only the owner of the installation can change the thresholds.
